name: Notebuddy
tagline: One companion. A little care, every day.
description:
Meet one little companion and grow together through everyday care. Feed, play, rest, train and take walks, chat about your day, and keep your companion’s portraits in a growth album.

Choose a surprise companion, draw your own, or upload a photo or image. The canvas offers colors, an eraser and undo. Uploads accept PNG, JPEG and WebP up to 12 MiB and 16 megapixels, with each side at least 32 pixels. Your device prepares a PNG reference with a longest side of at most 1024 pixels. Choosing a file or preview does not call AI. Meet starts analysis followed by portrait generation. People, animals, plants and objects can inspire an illustrated companion. AI infers one of 9 species from visible shape and one of 8 elements from colors or motifs. Only the element is random without a clear cue. Ambiguous species interpretations require confirmation. Silhouette, limb count, face and markings take priority over generic species stereotypes. Results are an interpretation, not an exact copy or an identification of a person.

Walks hold up to 5 charges and recover one every 5 minutes, including time away. Each outing can be peaceful, bring 10, 20 or 30 XP, or lead to a monster encounter with a short 2D battle replay. Some peaceful walks become short AI stories with two choices and a personal ending. These stories add no XP or items. One AI request prepares both endings; choosing or reopening does not request AI again. If AI is unavailable, a prepared story keeps the walk playable. Growth milestones are levels 1, 10, 30 and 50.

Successful care can bring a short AI reply from your companion. Care is saved before the reply, so an AI failure never undoes your action. Chat, care replies, walk stories, reference-image checks and portrait generation use your Anna AI allowance; checking a drawing or photo and generating its portrait are separate requests. Failed requests may still use allowance. Random starts use a ready-made baby portrait without an automatic image-generation request.

English by default, with an optional Korean interface. Your progress, recent chat, resized drawing/photo references and visual descriptions and saved portraits stay in Anna Persistent Storage. Start over clears the old companion, chat and portraits and returns to the first-meeting screen, where you choose a name and a random companion or a drawing/photo. Saved game data can also be removed separately. A failed custom-portrait attempt keeps the same companion for retry; a received image can retry saving without another generation while the window remains open. No external API key or local image-generation setup is needed.

Pixel RPG dungeons: when no dungeon is pending, each walk has a 25% chance to discover Hellgate, Ice Kingdom or Dream Forest. Discoveries last 24 hours. Each expedition has 3–6 rooms, with different enemies, recovery sanctuaries in longer layouts, and a final guardian. Health carries between rooms; a sanctuary restores up to half your maximum health. Movement follows the visible tiled corridors, and doors open after a room is cleared. Watch the camera follow your companion, pause playback, switch to 3x speed or skip to the saved result. A defeat or draw ends that attempt. Entry costs one walk charge for the whole expedition. Only a complete clear awards 10 cosmetic coins per region per Korea calendar day. There is no shop yet. The complete result is saved before playback, so closing or replaying never charges again or duplicates rewards. Clear or let the discovery expire before finding another dungeon.

A 64 by 64 pixel portrait is prepared locally from the completed companion portrait without additional AI usage. In dungeons, a four-direction animated pixel avatar uses the companion's species and colors sampled from its portrait. This is a simplified species-based avatar, not an AI-generated turnaround or an exact reproduction of custom artwork details. Dungeon rooms, movement and these avatar poses make no image-generation request. Existing single-boss expedition records remain replayable.
